What this shapes in your assignments:

Both tickets are boundary defects in small pure functions: an off-by-one at the age-65 comparison, and an off-by-one at the loop bound that drops the last stop. The fix surface for each is expected to be a single line. Do not let spec agents inflate a boundary fix into an architectural change: for stories of this shape, openspec's elaboration is mostly about pinning down which side of the boundary is correct (is 65 senior or adult; is the final stop inclusive), not about proposing splits. A story split across these two codelines is almost never warranted — they share no code.

The real spec risk here is test coverage, not requirements ambiguity. Both defects survived because the existing suites do not exercise the boundary. speckit's testability criteria are therefore high value on both stories: the acceptance criteria should name the exact boundary cases (the age immediately below, at, and above the threshold; a route rendered down to and including its terminus) so the vitest suites gain assertions that would have caught the original bug. Weight speckit accordingly rather than treating these as "simple elaboration only".

Note also that this project has minted a separate investigator per codeline (mocka-detective, mockb-detective) precisely because the reported cause of each defect is an unverified survey lead — nobody has yet confirmed the actual comparison operator in src/fares.ts or the actual loop bound in formatStops. Spec agents must therefore write acceptance criteria in terms of observable behaviour (which fare a 65-year-old is charged; which stops appear on the board), not in terms of a presumed operator or index. If a story's notes or AC assert a specific line-level cause, treat that as a gap for speckit to flag, not as settled fact.
